labels.text: Type a message and press Enter to send.

S13.01.needs: a signed-in account to see a reply
steps: Start agi in a terminal and wait for the main screen.
The composer at the bottom has focus; type: hello there
Press Enter.
Look: the text appears in the chat as your message, and a reply starts (needs a signed-in account).
S13.01.where: Main screen > composer box at the bottom > type a message > Enter

S13.02.note: Whether Shift+Enter arrives depends on the terminal; the code says Ctrl-J is the fallback.
steps: Type: line one
Press Shift+Enter, then type: line two.
Look: the composer shows two lines and nothing was sent.
Press Enter, then check the chat: the message keeps its line break.
S13.02.where: Main screen > composer box > Shift+Enter (also Alt+Enter or Ctrl-J)

S13.03.note: The 8-row cap is in code (composer_content_rows); the scrolling behaviour was not checked against the code path.
steps: Type one line, then press Shift+Enter and type another line.
Repeat until there are about ten lines.
Look: the composer grows one row per line up to about 8 text rows, then stops growing and the text scrolls inside it.
S13.03.where: Main screen > composer box > keep adding lines with Shift+Enter

labels.text: No editor is set; set VISUAL or EDITOR.

S13.05.needs: a VISUAL or EDITOR environment variable set
S13.05.note: This opens an external editor, not a full-screen editor inside the app; the help line was found in command_registry.rs but where it shows on screen was not traced.
steps: Before starting agi, set VISUAL or EDITOR in the shell (for example export EDITOR=nano).
Type a draft in the composer.
Press Ctrl-G; the editor opens with the draft.
Edit the text, save and quit the editor.
Look: the edited text is back in the composer. If no editor is set, look for the notice: No editor is set; set VISUAL or EDITOR.
S13.05.where: Main screen > composer box > Ctrl-G (or Ctrl-E) opens your $VISUAL or $EDITOR

labels.text: Type a message and press Enter to send.

S13.06.note: Expected a visible send button with a disabled reason; the code has only the Enter key, and an empty Enter does nothing with no message.
steps: Type a message.
Look for a visible send button; none was found in the code.
Press Enter.
Look: the message is sent and appears in the chat. Then press Enter on an empty composer and look for a reason; none is shown.
S13.06.where: Main screen > composer box > Enter (there is no send button)

labels.text: working, Esc or Ctrl-C to cancel

S13.07.needs: a signed-in account to get a streamed reply
S13.07.note: There is no on-screen stop button; the stop is the key.
steps: Send a prompt that gives a long answer (needs a signed-in account).
While the reply streams, look at the line that says: working, Esc or Ctrl-C to cancel.
Press Esc.
Look: the reply stops, the text already written stays, and the line: Stopped appears with the notice stopped the turn.
S13.07.where: While a reply is working > Esc (or Ctrl-C)

S13.09.note: Code comment says Shift+Enter never arrives in terminals without the keyboard protocol; Alt+Enter and Ctrl-J also add a newline.
steps: Type: first part
Press Shift+Enter.
Type: second part.
Look: a new line is added and the message is not sent.

S13.10.note: Expected Cmd+Z and Ctrl+Z; the code binds undo to Ctrl-_, Ctrl-7 and Ctrl-Shift-- (composer_edits.rs is_undo_key), not Ctrl+Z or Cmd+Z.
steps: Type a sentence, then delete part of it.
Press Ctrl-_ (Ctrl-Shift-- also undoes).
Look: the text goes back to the earlier state.
Press Ctrl-Shift-Z.
Look: the edit is reapplied.
S13.10.where: Main screen > composer box > Ctrl-_ to undo, Ctrl-Shift-Z to redo

labels.text: Attach the image on the clipboard

S13.11.note: Only clipboard images become attachments with Ctrl+V; pasted file paths arrive as text, and no file-paste attachment path was found.
steps: Copy a sentence, switch to agi and paste it into the composer; look: the text appears.
Copy an image (for example a screenshot), then press Ctrl+V in the composer.
Look: a chip line above the composer starts with a paperclip and ends with: /attach remove to drop, and the notice says attached.
S13.11.where: Main screen > composer box > Cmd+V (text) or Ctrl+V (clipboard image)

labels.text: Long pastes collapse to [Pasted text #N]; the full text is sent

S13.14.needs: some long text on the clipboard
S13.14.note: The marker is inline text, not an attachment; the limits are in composer_edits.rs (800 characters, 3 lines).
steps: Copy about 10 lines of text.
Paste it into the composer (Cmd+V).
Look: the composer shows one marker such as [Pasted text #1 +10 lines] instead of all the text.
Press Enter and check the chat: the full text was sent.
S13.14.where: Main screen > composer box > paste a long text (more than 3 lines or 800 characters)

S13.15.note: The draft size is not shown; the footer token and context counts are off by default (show_context false).
steps: Start a chat and have a few exchanges.
Look at the header's second row for a context meter with a percent.
Type a long draft without sending.
Look: the meter does not change with the draft length; it reflects the conversation so far. In Local mode the label begins with catalog estimate:.
S13.15.where: Main screen > header, second row > context meter

S13.19.note: No search key for prompt history was found (Ctrl-R is not bound); only Up and Down.
steps: Send three different prompts.
With the composer empty, press Up.
Look: the last sent prompt appears in the composer.
Press Up again, then Down, and check that the earlier and later prompts come back.
S13.19.where: Main screen > composer box > Up arrow and Down arrow

S13.21.note: Tab fills only the command name, not the template body; the body is sent when the command runs.
steps: Before starting, add a command file under .agiworkforce/commands/ in the project (for example review-note.md).
Type / in the composer and find your command in the Commands list.
Press Tab on it.
Look: the composer shows the command name (for example /review-note), then type your text after it and press Enter.
Look: the command runs with your text.
S13.21.where: Main screen > composer box > type / > pick a custom command in the Commands list > Tab

steps: With the composer empty, type /.
Look: a Commands list opens over the chat.
Type mo to filter the list, then move with Up and Down.
Look: the list narrows to matching commands; Enter runs the highlighted one and Tab fills it into the composer.

labels.text: No skills found. Add .md files to .agiworkforce/skills/

S13.23.note: Skills are invoked by typing their slash name; no skill picker was found.
steps: Type /skills and press Enter to list installed skills.
Look: the list starts with Skills (N): or, with none, the notice No skills found.
Type / and find the skill name in the Commands list.
Type the skill name, then your request, and press Enter.
Look: the reply follows the skill's instructions.
S13.23.where: Main screen > composer box > type / then the skill name (or /skills to list them)

labels.text: Hand the message to one of your agents

S13.24.needs: an agent set up in the workspace
S13.24.note: Agent entries in the Files popup were not traced to their display text; the agent names come from mention_candidates.
steps: Make sure an agent is set up in the workspace.
Type @ and look for the Files list; agents should appear in it.
Choose the agent and type your message, then press Enter.
Look: the message is handed to that agent and its reply appears.
S13.24.where: Main screen > composer box > type @ > pick an agent in the Files list, or type @agent-<name>

labels.text: Type to filter · ↑↓ to move · Enter to insert · Esc to cancel
Inline a file, or list a folder with @dir/

S13.26.needs: a trusted folder (an untrusted folder sends only the path)
S13.26.note: The trust rule (only the path is sent when the folder is untrusted) was confirmed in mentions.rs for folders; the same rule for files was not traced.
steps: Type @ and then part of a file name, for example README.
Look: the Files list narrows; press Enter on the file.
Look: the @file token is inserted into the composer.
Send a question about it and check the reply uses the file contents.
S13.26.where: Main screen > composer box > type @ > pick a file in the Files list > Enter

labels.text: Inline a file, or list a folder with @dir/

S13.27.needs: a trusted folder (an untrusted folder sends only the path)
S13.27.note: Whether folder entries show a trailing slash in the list was not verified.
steps: Type @ and then a folder name, for example src.
Pick the folder entry in the Files list and press Enter.
Look: the @folder/ token is inserted.
Send a question and check the reply lists or uses the folder contents.
S13.27.where: Main screen > composer box > type @ > pick a folder > Enter

labels.text: Ways to add context to your next message:

S13.30.needs: a connected MCP server that offers resources
S13.30.note: The @ popup lists workspace files only, so the connector syntax is not shown on screen; the rule is in agent/mod.rs mcp_resource_selectors.
steps: Connect an MCP server that offers resources (via /mcp).
Type @<server>:<resource-uri> in the composer and press Enter.
Look: the notices in the chat say what was attached, and the reply uses the resource.
S13.30.where: Main screen > composer box > type @server:resource-uri (typed by hand, no popup)

S13.31.note: Only attachments and generated images appear as chips; no skill, project, folder or page chips were found, and removal is by command, not a per-chip x.
steps: Type /attach followed by the path of an image file and press Enter.
Look: a chip line above the composer lists the file and says /attach remove to drop.
Type /attach remove and press Enter.
Look: the chip line is gone.
S13.31.where: Main screen > composer box > /attach <file> > chip line above the composer > /attach remove

labels.text: Ways to add context to your next message:

S13.35.note: No plus button was found; the attach menu is printed text, not a control.
steps: Type /attach and press Enter.
Look: the chat shows the list Ways to add context to your next message: with @path, @agent-<name>, /attach <file>, Ctrl+V and /mcp.
S13.35.where: Main screen > composer box > type /attach > Enter

labels.text: Dictate into the composer without sending
dictation added to the composer, Enter to send

S13.36.note: No microphone button was found; it is a command only.
steps: Type /dictate and press Enter (an optional language code may follow).
Speak when the app asks you to.
Finish the dictation as the prompt says.
Look: the words appear in the composer, are not sent, and the notice says dictation added to the composer, Enter to send.
S13.36.where: Main screen > composer box > type /dictate > Enter

labels.text: Voice mode requires a working microphone.

S13.37.needs: a microphone and speakers, and a signed-in account
S13.37.note: Voice mode leaves the composer and runs its own loop; there is no button for it.
steps: Type /voice and press Enter.
Wait for voice mode to take over the terminal, then speak.
Listen for the spoken reply.
End the voice session as the prompt says.
Look: the notice Voice session ended. appears back in the main screen.
S13.37.where: Main screen > composer box > type /voice > Enter (alias /v)

S13.40.needs: a signed-in account and a long-running reply
S13.40.note: Expected guidance that steers the running task; the code queues the message and sends it after the turn ends, so it does not steer the running task.
steps: Send a prompt that takes a while.
While the line shows working, type: use the tests folder, then press Enter.
Look: the line shows the draft with (Enter to queue, /btw to ask aside) and 1 message queued.
Wait for the turn to end and check that the queued message is then sent.
S13.40.where: While a reply is working > composer box > type a message > Enter

S13.41.needs: a signed-in account for the answer
S13.41.note: The side query is built from a copy of the session messages (agent/chat.rs side_query); the no-change result was not run.
steps: Start a long reply.
While it works, type /btw what does this file do? and press Enter.
Look: the notice answering the side question appears and a chat line starting btw: shows the answer.
Check that the main reply continues and the main conversation is not changed (for example /status shows the same Turns count).
S13.41.where: While a reply is working (or any time) > composer box > /btw <question> > Enter
